newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher on cool weather jitters.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher on cool weather jitters.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures ended higher on Tuesday on forecasts for continued cool, wet weather in the eastern U.S. Midwest which could cut soft red winter wheat yield potential, pit sources said.

"The ratings you saw this week are the best we're likely to see for the rest of the growing season," a floor trader said. "If we don't get some drier weather over there, this crop isn't going to produce what (USDA) thought it would."
The U.S. Agriculture Department in May put U.S. soft red winter wheat production at roughly 409 million bushels, versus last year's actual production of 422 million bushels.

"The wheat crop is one-and-a-half to three weeks behind schedule in growth stage and the cool temperatures, especially at night, are holding it back," said Licking County Extension agronomist Patrick Lipps in his weekly crop pathology report.
Ohio historically is the leading SRW wheat producer.

Concerns for scab and other wheat diseases mounted as the cool weather persisted, and long-range forecasts offered little reprieve. The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook called for below to much below normal temperatures.
Wheat futures ended 1-1/4 to 1/4 cent per bushel higher with July up 1-1/4 at $3.62 a bushel.

The harvest pace in the southern U.S. Plains also drew some bullish reviews. Traders noted three percent of the Texas wheat crop was harvested as of Sunday, according to the weekly USDA crop update. Last year at this time, 11 percent of the crop was harvested.
But gains were limited by an improvement in the winter wheat crop seen in USDA's weekly crop update.

USDA rated the winter wheat crop 55 percent good or excellent, 31 percent fair, 10 percent poor and four percent very poor. That was an improvement over the previous week when the crop was rated 51 percent good to excellent.
Weakness in soybeans also capped the upward momentum.
On the day, LIT bought three million bushels July while Merrill Lynch and SAK Futures each bought 1.5 million July.
Merrill Lynch sold two million September and Smith Barney sold one million September.
In options trade, LIT sold 400 July $3.60 puts at eight cents, pit sources said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 12,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 14,196.
